scenes.heading: Transforming graphs
scenes.sub: Move it, stretch it, flip it
scenes.say: Know a few basic graphs, and you can draw thousands more. Today you'll learn to move, stretch and flip any graph in this chapter.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A photo app lets you move, stretch and flip a picture
scenes.science: Translate, dilate and reflect a basic graph
scenes.breaks: In a photo app, dragging right is "plus". In an equation, moving right 3 shows up as (x − 3).
scenes.say: Think of editing a photo on your phone. You can move it, stretch it and flip it, but it's still the same picture. Graphs work the same way. Start with a shape you know, then move, stretch or flip it.

scenes.heading: Translations
scenes.say: Start with the dashed parabola, y equals x squared. Adding two outside moves it up two. Now y equals x minus three, all squared: inside the bracket, so it moves sideways, and minus three means right three.
scenes.caption: Start with the dashed parabola y = x². Adding 2 outside moves it up 2. y = (x − 3)² changes the inside, so it moves sideways: minus 3 means right 3.

scenes.heading: Reflections
scenes.say: Here's y equals two to the x. Put a minus in front of the whole function and it flips upside down: a reflection in the x-axis. Replace x with negative x and it flips left to right: a reflection in the y-axis.
scenes.caption: y = 2ˣ. A minus in front of the whole function flips it upside down: a reflection in the x-axis. Replacing x with −x flips it left to right: a reflection in the y-axis.

scenes.heading: The full toolkit
scenes.say: Put it all together: y equals a times f of x minus h, plus k. The a stretches the graph from the x-axis, and a negative a flips it. Then h moves it right and k moves it up. Dilate and reflect first, then translate.

scenes.heading: Describe the transformation
scenes.question: How is y = x² transformed to y = −2(x − 1)² + 3?
scenes.say: The two is a dilation by factor two from the x-axis. The minus sign reflects it in the x-axis. Then x minus one moves it one right, and plus three moves it three up. The turning point is one, three.
scenes.caption: 2: dilation by factor 2 from the x-axis. The minus reflects it in the x-axis. (x − 1) moves it 1 right and + 3 moves it 3 up. Turning point (1, 3).

scenes.say: Quick recap. Outside changes move up and down as written; inside changes move sideways the opposite way. A stretches, a minus flips. Dilate and reflect, then translate. Now try the practice questions!
